decision: Deploy KonnectYatra to production at konnectyatra.org using a symlinked public_html -> ~/konnectyatra/public, with GitHub Actions SSH auto-deploy on push to main
reasoning: Main-domain docroot is locked to public_html; symlink keeps app code out of the web root and URLs clean. Host has SSH+Composer, so Actions-over-SSH gives true push-to-deploy without exposing tokens in the repo.
expected_outcome: Pushing to main updates the live site in ~30s with no manual steps; data seeded from local XAMPP dump

decision: Rebuilt the Yatri booking flow: 19 airport-based Gurpurab packages from the pricing sheet (old ones disabled via new package.status column), cascading origin selector, fuller apply form (nationality, WebP doc uploads, yatri_documents table), admin-configured Payment Settings shown on the payment page, Pay Later email + 30-day validity, unique date/time Yatri IDs, and Yatri Booking Form print/PDF export (dompdf + FPDI)
reasoning: Client supplied the airport pricing sheet and booking-form design; needed accurate per-origin packages, complete applicant records, configurable payment instructions, and printable/exportable booking forms bundling uploaded documents
expected_outcome: Bookings capture full data with unique IDs; staff can configure payments and export complete Yatri forms with documents; new schema/seed/deps must be applied on production at deploy

decision: Bundle a 42,741-row US ZIP table in the repo instead of calling a live ZIP lookup API
reasoning: Gurdwara ZIP search and the Address Book both need ZIP -> city/coords. A free API (zippopotam.us) needs no setup but makes a public production page depend on a third party staying up. A bundled CSV + seeder costs 1.45MB in git and one prod seed command, and is then instant and offline-proof.
expected_outcome: ZIP search and Address Book keep working regardless of any third-party outage; no API keys or billing to manage

decision: Use keyless Google Maps links for the Address Book rather than the paid Places API
reasoning: Rashad needs to find gurdwaras that are not yet in the database while in the field. Places API auto-flags what is missing but needs a Google Cloud key with billing (~$32/1k searches); a Maps search button centred on his GPS plus the normal Add form costs nothing and ships immediately.
expected_outcome: Rashad can still discover and add missing gurdwaras on site, at zero cost; revisit only if manual adding proves too slow

decision: Merge the client gurdwara sheet onto existing rows and keep extras, rather than replacing the table
reasoning: The 151-row sheet has no photos or sangat sizes, abbreviated names ('Gurd ...') and typos, and only 33 of the 43 existing rows matched it. A straight replace would have destroyed 17 photos and put typo'd names on the public site.
expected_outcome: 43 -> 150 gurdwaras with all photos and sangat data intact; blank sheet cells never overwrite good stored values

decision: Drive the admin package form's State and Departure Airport dropdowns from the departure_origins table, and save package.state_code on create/edit, instead of the hard-coded state list
reasoning: The form carried 26 hand-typed state options copied from PdfPackagesSeeder, so origins added later (Austria, Belgium) never appeared. Worse, the form had no state_code field and neither create() nor edit() wrote it -- but /all-packages filters on state_code, so every package created through the admin UI was invisible on the public page. departure_origins is already the admin-managed source of truth for the public cascade selector.
expected_outcome: Origins added under Departure Origins show up in the package form immediately, and packages created in admin appear on /all-packages under the chosen airport

decision: Add a Copy Package action that duplicates a package (plus its itinerary and price-breakdown rows) and opens the copy in the edit form, giving the copy its own duplicated flyer file
reasoning: Rashad builds most new packages from an existing one -- roughly 80% is identical and only the departure, fares and brochure change, so retyping the whole form was the bulk of the work. The copy needs its own flyer file because edit() unlinks the previous image whenever the brochure changes, so a shared filename would delete the original package's image. The copy inherits status because the package form has no status control -- a hidden copy could never be enabled.
expected_outcome: Creating a departure variant takes a click plus three edits instead of retyping the form; no package can destroy another package's brochure

decision: Add an Active/Hidden Status control to the package form and a Hidden badge on the package list
reasoning: The public packages page renders only status=1, but nothing in the admin ever set or displayed status, so a package could be invisible with no way to see why or fix it. This is what hid the Amsterdam/Netherlands package: it was created by Copy from a disabled package and inherited status=0. It also made Copy unsafe, since a copy inherits the original's status.
expected_outcome: A package is never silently invisible -- hidden ones are badged in the list and can be switched to Active from the edit form

decision: Homepage popup collects 'Near Gurdwara Sahib' leads (name, phone, address, nearest Gurdwara, referral source) and emails rm@konnectyatra.org
reasoning: Rashad wants to capture visitor contact + their nearest Gurdwara Sahib for outreach; shows once per homepage load, only stops once the visitor actually submits (closing the popup does not suppress it on the next visit)
expected_outcome: New gurdwara_leads DB table + admin list at /admin/gurdwara-leads; grows the same kind of gurdwara/contact data used by the Address Book and master-list work

decision: Serve /sitemap.xml from a dynamic Laravel route (SitemapController) instead of a static file, and tighten robots.txt
reasoning: The site had no sitemap at all and robots.txt was wide open (bare 'Disallow:'), so uploaded passport/greencard/licence/photo folders were crawlable and admin/user areas were not excluded. A static sitemap file would go stale every time Rashad adds a package, gurdwara or blog post; a route regenerates from the DB on every request and applies the same visibility gates as the public pages (package status=1, blog status=published).
expected_outcome: Search Console can be given one URL that always reflects current content; no uploaded visitor documents in the index

decision: Expand the homepage Gurdwara Sahib popup to collect middle name, father's name, email, and number of Yatris interested, plus an Others option for how they heard about Konnect Yatra USA
reasoning: Client asked for a fuller lead record: the original 8-field form did not capture enough to identify a person (no father's name, the standard identity field in this community), had no email for follow-up, and gave no sense of group size. Others was missing from the source pills, so anyone who found the site another way had to pick a wrong answer
expected_outcome: Leads arrive with enough detail to follow up by email and gauge group size before calling; new columns nullable so the existing submissions stay readable

decision: Rebuild /special-package and its apply step on a shared design-token stylesheet, using an itinerary-spine layout with a running total that becomes a fixed action bar on mobile
reasoning: The configurator was a flat Bootstrap grid: the six included days rendered in slate boxes styled as .disabled so the itinerary read as unavailable, the optional days hid their surcharge until the total silently changed, and the price plus the only CTA sat stranded at the bottom of a 3400px page. The apply step then asked for ~40 fields per traveller with no reminder of what had been configured. Both pages now share public/new-assets/css/special-land-package.css (primitive -> semantic -> component tokens) so they read as one flow.
expected_outcome: Travellers can see what each extra day costs before adding it, keep the running total in view while configuring, and carry a journey recap into the application; both pages stay legible down to 390px

decision: Publish sitewide Schema.org JSON-LD from a central PHP builder (app/Support/Schema.php + config/schema.php) rather than per-view hand-written blocks, and type the business as TravelAgency rather than separate Organization + LocalBusiness nodes
reasoning: The site had zero structured data and one shared title/description across all 224 sitemap URLs. A central builder keeps the Organization/WebSite entity identical on every page and linked by @id; splitting Organization and LocalBusiness into two nodes would fork the business entity. config/ over a DB table avoids a prod migration.
expected_outcome: Google and LLM crawlers resolve konnectyatra.org to one business with a Jamaica NY address; package, gurdwara, hotel, blog and event pages become individually understandable; breadcrumb and sitelink eligibility in SERPs

decision: Put the business NAP facts (address, phone, email, map lat/lng, opening hours, sameAs profiles) behind an Admin > SEO Settings > Business Details screen backed by biz_* keys in site_settings, and make the header, footer, Contact page, homepage and JSON-LD all read them through App\Support\Business
reasoning: The schema needed facts only the owner has (coordinates, hours, social profiles), and the address was hard-coded in five separate views — so NAP consistency depended on remembering to edit all of them, which is the most common reason a site fails to match its Google Business Profile. site_settings already exists, so this needed no migration.
expected_outcome: Rashad can fill in coordinates and hours himself; editing the address in one admin field updates every page and the structured data at once; NAP can no longer silently drift

decision: Store each booking's surcharge amounts on the booking row, while keeping the rates admin-editable in site_settings
reasoning: The printed Konnect.US application adds four fees (wheelchair for the whole trip, Indian passport processing, Wagah two-suitcase baggage, late application). Rashad must be able to change a rate without a developer or a deploy, but recomputing an existing booking from the current rates would silently restate a total the yatri already agreed to and paid. Rates and charged amounts are therefore different things and are stored separately.
expected_outcome: Rates change from the admin with no migration or deploy; historical bookings keep the totals they were quoted; the admin list, PDF and booking emails can all show the same figures without recomputing

decision: Target the 15 USA keywords as four intents on four pages, sending the agency terms to the home page rather than /aboutus
reasoning: Page one for the head terms is entirely Pakistan-based inbound operators who cannot serve a US departure, so the differentiator is the word USA — which appeared in no title or heading. The 15 terms are near-synonyms: one page each would have them cannibalising one another. The agency cluster goes to the home page because the SERP rewards package hubs over company profiles, and /aboutus holds only 204 words.
expected_outcome: The four owner pages rank for their own cluster without competing; impressions appear for USA-qualified queries that previously returned nothing; no page loses ground on the destination terms it already ranks for

decision: Fill the 17 location pages with US-origin practical content rather than more history, and ship it as an idempotent seeder
reasoning: Every locations.description was empty, so the pages were stubs. Everything ranking for the shrine terms is written for someone already inside Pakistan or for an Indian pilgrim crossing at Wagah; none address a yatri flying from the USA. Visit duration, ground underfoot, wheelchair viability, crowd timing and what to carry are the gap, and they are what the booking form already collects. A shared etiquette block repeated 17 times was rejected as duplicate content across a page set.
expected_outcome: The four priority shrine pages start appearing for their own named terms (Nankana Sahib Yatra, Panja Sahib Yatra, Gurdwara Dera Sahib Lahore Tour); enquiries mention details only these pages give; no page set is flagged as doorway content

decision: Show and store the admin yatri date fields in DD-MMM-YYYY, and normalise whatever is submitted on save
reasoning: The four date fields on admin/yatri-visa-edit were native <input type="date">, which draws in the browser's locale and posts YYYY-MM-DD. The columns are varchar and already held four formats (14-AUG-1947, 1960-07-25, 06-18-2026, 1 Apr 2025), so the admin form was adding a fifth. DD-MMM-YYYY is unambiguous to a US reader and is already what the public apply form writes.
expected_outcome: Dates read the same everywhere a yatri record is shown, and each record saved through the admin converges on one format without a migration

decision: Let the admin enter a booking by hand and print a blank application form, both off the same template
reasoning: Rashad needs to add candidates himself and to hand out a paper form people fill in by pen. Keeping edit/create as one blade and filled/blank as one PDF template means the sheet someone writes on and the fields the admin types are the same list in the same order, so transcribing is reading down the page and the two cannot drift as fields are added.
expected_outcome: Paper applications get keyed in without missing fields; adding a field once updates both the screen and the printed sheet

decision: Upload the Zelle QR code in Payment Settings rather than committing it, and reuse balance.raseed_no as the transaction number
reasoning: The QR is the client's banking artefact and changes with the account, so it belongs in a field he controls, gitignored, alongside the Zelle name/phone/email keys already in site_settings. The receipt number staff already enter against a payment is the transaction number, so printing it needs no new column and no prod migration.
expected_outcome: Rashad swaps the code himself when the account changes; a paid booking prints its own confirmation number back to the traveller

decision: Give the Quick Yatri application form its own quick_yatris table and admin module rather than extending yatri_visas
reasoning: The printed Konnect.US sheet is the client's source of truth and changes on its own schedule; folding it into yatri_visas would mean bending 40-odd paper fields onto a schema built for the booking/visa/payment pipeline, and every future revision of the sheet would risk that pipeline. A standalone table mirrors the paper column for column and touches nothing existing.
expected_outcome: Rashad can key in and print applications immediately; revisions to the printed form become edits to one template and one table, with no risk to bookings

decision: Site-wide Markdown content negotiation (Accept: text/markdown), a dynamic /llms.txt guide, and a /privacy trust-anchor page, to raise the Is Agentic (Ora/Vercel) audit score
reasoning: Ora's public audit flagged three checks: no Accept: text/markdown negotiation (Vary missing Accept), no agent-instruction file with when-to-use guidance, and Privacy missing from the About/Contact/Privacy trust-anchor set. Built a global NegotiateMarkdown middleware (skips /admin and /user) that converts the rendered #content region to Markdown via league/html-to-markdown, honours Accept q-values per RFC 9110, 406s when neither html nor markdown is acceptable, and always sets Vary: Accept. /llms.txt is a route (same pattern as /sitemap.xml) reading live from Business:: and Package::status=1 so it can't drift. /privacy follows the aboutus/contactus template, added to the footer and sitemap.
expected_outcome: curl -H 'Accept: text/markdown' on any public page returns a clean Markdown document with the right Content-Type and Vary header; agents reading /llms.txt get explicit when-to-use guidance; About/Contact/Privacy all verify. Should move the three failing/partial Ora checks to pass.

decision: Quick Yatri sheet: a live USA-airport dropdown for the Round Trip route, merged instruction 2/3, and real tick boxes on all three option bars in every mode
reasoning: Rashad marked up the printed/blank form: the Round Trip box was hard-coded to one route (PHL-ISB/LHE-PHL, PA/DE/NJ-SO) with no way to pick another departure airport; instruction 3 ('2 Pages of Indian Passport') needed to read as part of instruction 2; and the wheelchair/wheelchair-full-trip/meal-preference bars had no box to tick on the printed blank sheet, only in entry/print (an open question flagged when the sheet first shipped 2026-08-21).
expected_outcome: New nullable departure_airport_code column, entry mode gets a <select> of active USA departure_origins airports (same table the public packages selector reads, with a preserved '(current)' option if a since-deactivated code is already stored, matching the package-form pattern), blank mode gets a qy-rule writing line since paper can't offer a dropdown, print mode shows the resolved airport + state. Verified via headless-Chrome screenshot that page 1 still fits with room above the signature line — the merged instruction bullet actually freed more space than the new boxes cost, so no extra spacing changes were needed.

decision: Quick Yatri page 2: 4 wording corrections from Rashad's marked-up terms page
reasoning: Rashad marked up the printed Yatri Application & Travel Instructions page: 'Indian Passport Holders' needed '2 Pages of' before 'passport' (same fix as page 1's instruction list); the baggage fee now applies at one suitcase too, not just two, so the heading dropped 'Two-' and the body reads 'one or two suitcases'; the ancestral-village-visit approval gained a reason ('due to security reasons'); and the itinerary-change list gained 'rescheduled' alongside changed/amended/canceled.
expected_outcome: Confirmed with Rashad before editing (listed the four corrections and the one ambiguous reading first, per his request) rather than guessing silently. All four verified in a headless-Chrome screenshot of the printed page 2 and in a new PHPUnit test.

decision: Quick Yatri blank form: an airport picker that pre-fills Round Trip on the printed sheet, plus a redesigned footer (Uploads/Signature/Zelle QR)
reasoning: Rashad's representatives hand out blank sheets at regional signup events (e.g. Miami) where every candidate departs from the same airport, so the Round Trip line needed to show that airport (e.g. MIA/FL) instead of a blank line every time. Separately, the footer's Price-guarantee and Zelle-instructions bullets were superseded by a scannable QR, and the fixed 50pt QR was too small for a phone camera to read reliably off a printout.
expected_outcome: Download Blank Form on the Quick Yatri list gained an airport dropdown that rewrites the download link's ?airport= query string; QuickYatriController::blank() validates it against active USA departure_origins and pre-fills the in-memory (unsaved) row. New App\Support\GurdwaraGeo::stateAbbreviation() turns a departure_origins state label into a 2-letter code for the compact CODE/ST format. The footer now reads the same pay_zelle_qr Payment Settings upload the dompdf yatri_form already uses, at a 115pt box (~1.6in, reliably scannable) matched by an equal-size Signature box with its label bottom-aligned; the two removed bullets and the option-bar checkboxes/borders were resized/added per Rashad's marked-up screenshots. Verified with headless-Chrome screenshots at every size step, since page 1 is a fixed 11in box and the footer is the last thing on it.

decision: Quick Yatri footer: three matched bordered panels (frontend-design pass), plus auto-formatted phone/name/email on print
reasoning: The footer still read as sparse after the box resize — Uploads sat as a short bare list next to two tall boxes, leaving visible dead space at the foot of the page. Separately, printed records showed raw data exactly as typed: an 11-digit phone string, ALL CAPS names (common when staff type from a passport), and mixed-case email.
expected_outcome: Ran the frontend-design skill scoped to just the footer region (kept the sheet's existing navy/orange/red brand system rather than inventing a new one). Uploads is now a bordered panel matching Signature/QR's footprint, header-top/checklist-middle/date-bottom via justify-content:space-between, so it fills its height instead of clustering at the top. New $personName and $phone closures in _sheet-body.blade.php format print-mode only (Str::title() for names, a 10-digit-or-11-with-leading-1 check for phone, printing anything else exactly as typed rather than guessing); email is lowercased server-side in QuickYatriController::payload() on save, the correct single normalisation point since email is genuinely case-insensitive.

decision: Quick Yatri 'Travelling from' reads a bundled full US airport list (app/Support/UsAirports.php), not the departure_origins table
reasoning: The top bar now asks where the applicant is travelling from, which any of ~459 US commercial airports can answer. departure_origins is the short curated list of routes KonnectYatra actually sells and it drives the public packages selector, so expanding it to 400+ rows would wreck that page. A static class ships with the code, needs no seeder or migration, and works on prod the moment it deploys.
expected_outcome: Admins can pick any US airport for a Quick Yatri applicant; the public packages selector keeps its short curated origin list unchanged.

decision: Quick Yatri sheet: every free-text answer reads in CAPS, email stays lowercase, cell numbers read +1 (786) 516 2525
reasoning: Rashad asked for caps that do not depend on the typist having Caps Lock on. Done as a CSS text-transform applied by the $txt/$mail closures, so it holds while typing, on screen and in print, in all three sheet modes, and leaves the stored value untouched. This replaces the earlier Title Case treatment for person names - names are text, and all text is CAPS. Email is excluded because it gets read back and typed into a mail client.
expected_outcome: Printed sheets are legible however they were filled in; no stored data is re-cased, so the rule is reversible.

decision: Quick Yatri prices become editable in the admin (OW/RT/LP + wheelchair fee) with a per-applicant override
reasoning: The three grid prices were hard-coded in QuickYatri::TRIP_OPTIONS, so a fare change needed a deploy; and two yatris on the same trip option are not always quoted the same thing (group size, departure airport, a rate agreed at a gurdwara event). Grid prices go to site_settings (no migration, matches the standing 'settings belong in the admin' rule); the per-applicant price is a custom_price flag + price_note on the row so re-saving the sheet never puts the grid price back.
expected_outcome: The office moves a fare from the Quick Yatri toolbar without a developer, blank forms printed at events carry today's price, and a negotiated price survives both a re-save and a later grid change.

decision: Quick Yatri page-1 footer redesigned as a 60/40 notes+QR split; signature moved to the foot of page 2
reasoning: The old three-panel Uploads/Signature/QR row spent a third of the footer on tick boxes duplicating the document list page 2 already carries, and had the applicant signing above the terms rather than after them. Splitting 60/40 gives the conditions room to be read and lets the Zelle QR be a large square, which is what a phone camera needs off paper.
expected_outcome: The QR scans reliably off a printout, the conditions (now including the $500 minimum deposit) are legible at 9.2pt, and the signature sits after the terms it binds. Page 1 still prints as exactly two pages.

decision: Make the sheet's first printed condition editable from the Quick Yatri price dialog, capped at a measured 220 characters, and drop the per-traveller bullet from the page-1 box
reasoning: The bullet names a deadline and a late fee that move every season alongside the fares, so it belongs in the screen already opened when the season turns rather than a settings page of its own. It is printed into a fixed 11in page, so the length has to be bounded: removing the per-traveller bullet plus trimming the panel gap from 8pt to 7pt buys the first bullet a fifth line, and 220 characters is the most that fits five lines at the worst wrapping measured.
expected_outcome: The office re-dates or rewrites that sentence itself without a deploy, and no edit within the cap can push the sheet onto a third printed page
